newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves $219 mln in credits for Azerbaijan.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves $219 mln in credits for Azerbaijan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund Friday approved two credits totaling about $219 million for Azerbaijan to support the government's economic program for the next three years.
The Fund said of this amount, about $135 million was available under its enhanced structural adjustment facility and the remainder under the extended fund facility.

Azerbaijan's medium term program builds on macroeconomic progress already made and is designed to prepare the country for a prospective oil boom as production is projected to double by the turn of the century and to quadruple shortly thereafter, the fund said.
The program is designed to achieve annual growth of 5.1 percent in 1997, rising by 7.6 per cent in 1998 and 8.4 percent in 1999. Growth is estimated at 1.2 percent in the current year.
It also seeks to cut inflation from an estimated 19.9 percent in 1996 to 9.1 percent in 1997, 6.5 percent in 1998 and 6.2 percent by 1999.
In the area of structural reforms, the Fund said the highest priority areas are banking reform, privatization and the termination of the government's heavy in involvement in production and trade.
